name: Context Search
description: Context Search REST API (not MCP, no auth, Wix network): route a question to domains and retrieve KB context. See https://bo.wix.com/stash/dora-context-api-demo/
notes:
Findings from driving the API through this app via chrome-devtools-mcp (2026-09-09), verified live.

1. capabilities embeds the full request schema for both POST endpoints, verbatim -
   down to the source docstring on domain_ids / conversation_id / caller semantics
   (see result.filters in a capabilities call). That's more than the announcement
   shows and it can't drift from the code, so read it before any external doc.

2. /domains ranks ALL 181 domains, not just searchable ones. considered[] included
   is_searchable:false entries (suppliers_hub, user_success ranked #4/#5 for a
   restaurants query) - routing doesn't filter by searchability, retrieval does.
   rank is the domain's absolute position across all 181, not a 0..limit-1 index:
   a limit:3 response showed ranks 1, 3, 4.

3. DOMAIN_NOT_SEARCHABLE is real and reproducible. domain_ids:["ab_test"] (capabilities
   marks it is_searchable:false) -> transport 200, statusCode 400, body:
   {"success":false,"error":"Domain(s) have no published content to search: ab_test",
   "error_type":"DOMAIN_NOT_SEARCHABLE"}. This app's context_call() correctly
   surfaced it as isError despite the 200 - confirms the statusCode/body gotcha
   is real and the decode here is right.

4. Table names really do only arrive as prose. A KPI hit's content reads like:
   "...Sources: prod.rest.monthly_churn (Readiness status.); prod.rest.restaurants_gpv_dim
   (Order volume.)." No structured table field exists in the response.

5. include_answer:true is genuinely grounded, not a rubber stamp. Live model was
   accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash-0731. It cited only 1 of 5 retrieved
   chunks (chunks_used:5) and explicitly said what was MISSING from context rather
   than guessing - cited_doc_ids is a real subset of what it was given, not all of it.

6. A vague query did not trigger the documented "clarification" response. Tried
   "how is it going" expecting it - still routed normally (server_routed,
   multi_domain, 3 domains selected, top confidence only 0.79). Clarification
   exists per the docs but isn't as simple as "ask something vague" - didn't
   reproduce it in one try.

tools.name: context__capabilities
tools.description:
GET, no body, no auth. Call once per session, before searching: returns domain_count / searchable_domain_count, the kb_types vocabulary (product, business, analytical are searchable; reports and rules exist but are never embedded, so filtering to them always returns nothing), doc_kinds (object/property/rel), max_domain_ids, and doc_id_format. The response also embeds the full request JSON-schema for both POST endpoints under result.filters, straight from the source docstring - read that instead of any external doc, it can't drift from the code.

Example: no args needed - just Run.

tools.name: context__domains
tools.description:
POST. Where does this question live? Ranking only, no content retrieved - cheaper than context__search when you just want to see or confirm routing. Most callers should call context__search directly instead, since it routes internally too.

Ranks ALL domains, not just searchable ones: considered[] includes is_searchable:false entries mixed in below the searchable ones, and `rank` is each domain's absolute position across every domain, not a 0..limit-1 index - a limit:3 response can show ranks 1, 3, 4.

Example: {"query": "How many active restaurant order sites were there last month", "limit": 5} -> routing.selected includes "restaurants".

tools.name: context__search
tools.description:
POST. Routes (or uses domain_ids to skip routing) and retrieves matching context in one call - the one endpoint most callers actually need.

domain_ids supplied -> routing is skipped, exactly those domains are searched; if one is_searchable:false (check via context__capabilities first), you get statusCode 400 DOMAIN_NOT_SEARCHABLE - verified live with domain_ids:["ab_test"]: {"success":false,"error":"Domain(s) have no published content to search: ab_test","error_type":"DOMAIN_NOT_SEARCHABLE"}.

KPIs only: kb_types:["analytical"], doc_kinds:["object"] - the analytical KB embeds its relationships under the same kb_type, so doc_kinds is what narrows it.

Table names only ever arrive as prose inside a KPI's "Sources:" line (verified live) - there is no structured table field to filter or read.

include_answer:true adds an answer object {text, model, cited_doc_ids, chunks_used} synthesized over the retrieved chunks (live model: deepseek-v4-flash-0731). cited_doc_ids is the checked intersection of what the model cited and what it was actually given - safe to render as provenance. Off by default: summarizing passages beforehand throws away context you could have used yourself.

Gotcha: the gateway always answers transport HTTP 200 - the real status is `statusCode` inside the response; this tool (context_call() in serve.py) already decodes that, so isError in this UI reflects the real status.

Example: {"query": "How many active restaurant order sites were there last month", "limit": 5} -> results[0] is the KPI active_restaurants_orders_sites, Sources: prod.rest.monthly_churn, prod.rest.restaurants_gpv_dim.
